comment: Byte ceilings for what a COLD load pays before any route code runs. The CSS limits follow css_comment below; a JS limit rises only with a measurement in the PR that explains what the bytes buy.

apps/app.comment: Entry chunk + transitive STATIC imports + entry CSS. Lazy route chunks are excluded: they are paid on navigation, not on boot. Includes the route loader that resolves the shell's opening decision before first paint — it costs ~4.6 KB gzip and removes three full-viewport paints from a cold load, which is a trade worth making explicitly. React, React Router and Zod are split into vendor chunks: that costs ~600 B gzip in boundary overhead and buys cache stability, since an edit under lib/api used to invalidate React Router for every returning reader.
apps/app.css_comment: CSS limits (owner rule, 18 Nov 2026): each eager_css limit is the value measured after a debt audit plus a 10% buffer, rounded up. When a change exhausts the buffer, first audit and remove eager CSS debt (rules nothing renders, duplicate keyframes or transitions, hand-written CSS an emitted utility replaces, CSS only lazy routes use, which moves to their chunk), then re-measure and reset both limits to measured + 10%, with the before, after and new limits in the PR. Never raise a limit any other way. Current: 126779 B raw and 24324 B gzip measured on 20 Nov 2026 (PR #1082; owner, 2026-11-20, after the subtle 3D button style; reset to measured + 10%).
